1022-browse-academic-units-and-programs: Music Research: B.Mus. in Composition, Education, History, Theory and Music Studies; Minors in Applied Performance Sciences, History, Composition, Education, Entrepreneurship, Theory and Technology.
Performance: B.Mus. in Performance, Early Music and Jazz; L.Mus.; Minors in Conducting, Early Music, Jazz Arranging and Composition, and Jazz Performance. Approved for 2026–2027.
1022-department-of-music-research: Links applied performance sciences, composition, education, history, theory, technology and recording, treating musicianship, musical grammar and ideas as connected. Majors allow other interests; Music Studies suits individual plans. Analysis and writing skills also prepare you for law, journalism, management or librarianship.

The B.Mus./B.Ed. (170 credits) and Minor in Music Education (18) won't admit students in 2026–2027 during a review; admissions can suggest alternatives like Music Studies. Several minors are open to other faculties. Listed courses are required unless noted.
1022-prerequisite-courses-for-m-mus-in-s: Finish prerequisites before applying, and tell the Sound Recording Area first. Bachelor's students are encouraged to take them through the Musical Science and Technology Minor (p. 1032). See the program's site.
1023-b-mus-b-ed-bachelor-of-music-and-ba: Neither education program is accepting applications. The B.Ed. Music is 152 credits of teacher training toward Quebec certification, for B.Mus. holders, typically 2.5 years with Advanced Standing, through Education.

Without a B.Mus.: the 170-credit concurrent program (p. 1027), usually five years, with both degrees at one convocation, through Schulich. An F or J in Field Experience means Unsatisfactory Standing and withdrawal after finishing the term.
1023-program-description: Performance science for music practice, creation and teaching: optimal performance, healthy playing and singing, physical, psychological and social factors, and applied research.
1023-interdisciplinary-courses: 3 credits, when the topic is relevant.
1023-program-description-2: Classical composition for instruments and voices, with or without electronics, through lectures and private lessons in years 3 and 4, plus theory and history. Free electives allow a minor or breadth. B- minimum in Composition Area courses.
1024-prerequisite-courses: 22 credits. Auditions, placement tests or equivalents can exempt you.
1025-program-description: Techniques and aesthetics of contemporary instrumental and digital composition, with orchestration, history and theory.
1025-program-description-2: Interdisciplinary, in Classical and Jazz streams: core theory, history, musicianship and professional development, plus specializations in practical studies, entrepreneurship, education, technology, performance sciences, composition, theory or history.
1025-program-prerequisites-foundation-pr: Placement tests or equivalents can exempt you.
1026-music-history-2: 3–9 credits of MUHL or MUPP at 300+.
1026-music-education: 3–9 credits of MUGT, MUCT or MUIT at 200+.
1026-music-technology: 3–9 credits of MUMT or MUSR at 200+.
1028-prerequisite-courses: 4 of Large Ensemble, 6 of non-Music electives, and 22 from the list. Placement tests or equivalents can exempt you.
1029-program-description: Under review, with no new students from Fall 2026. Limited enrolment, open to all but concurrent B.Mus./B.Ed. students, with Schulich's approval, replacing free electives. Choose from one of three streams.
1030-program-description: With Desautels: building ventures and managing careers as performers, teachers and administrators, with marketing, fundraising, publicity and finance. For B.Mus. students after a year with CGPA 3.0. Limited; apply through Music Research. Can't combine with Desautels' Management, Marketing, Finance or Operations minors.
1030-complementary-courses-9-credits: 3, then 3–6, then 0–3 from three lists. Internships or projects must be approved as entrepreneurial.
1031-program-description: Music in cultural settings, musicians' social conditions, performing styles, and meaning and identity, across Western classical, jazz and popular idioms. Prepares for musicology, journalism, information science, arts administration and teaching. 92 credits, plus 32 Foundation for out-of-province students.
1031-history-2: 27 credits from Groups I, II and III, at least 6 from each.
1032-program-description: Open to all but Music History majors, replacing electives and some complementaries.
1032-program-description-2: Science and technology as applied to music.
1033-complementary-courses-6-credits: MUSR 300D1/D2 is limited, taken together, usually for the Sound Recording Qualifying Year; ask the Area Coordinator.
1033-program-description: Models and methods of musical languages: how pieces are built and how that generalizes, through writing and analysis. Specialties include mathematical models and Renaissance counterpoint.
1034-program-description: Open to all but Theory majors, with Schulich's approval, replacing free electives.
1035-department-of-performance: B.Mus., M.Mus., D.Mus., L.Mus., Graduate Diploma and Artist Diploma, with lessons for all instruments and voice, and large and small ensembles. They've played Maison symphonique, Koerner Hall, the National Arts Centre, Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center; many concerts are streamed, some on CBC.

Specializations: strings, guitar, harp, winds, brass, euphonium, percussion, piano, organ, harpsichord, voice, historical instruments, choral and instrumental conducting, and jazz (bass, drums, flute, guitar, piano, saxophone, trombone, trumpet, vibraphone, violin, voice).
1035-program-description: Practical and theoretical training, with individual lessons and ensembles. 91 credits, plus 34 Foundation for out-of-province students.
1035-special-requirements: B- minimum in practical instruction, exams and ensembles.
1035-prerequisite-courses: 22 credits. Auditions, placement tests or equivalents can exempt you. Keyboard principals skip MUSP 170 and 171.
1036-performance-2: Large Ensemble in the first four terms, then 8 and 4 credits from lists. MUEN courses can repeat.
1037-music-history-literature-performanc: MUHL or MUPP at 300+, and 3 more from MUHL or MUPP.
1037-program-description: Vocal pedagogy, coaching, languages, theory and musicology, with recitals, opera, early music, song, choirs, and the McGill Concerto and Wirth Vocal Competitions. 91 credits, plus 32 Foundation for out-of-province students.
1037-diction: Before or with these, show English Second Language, ITAL 205D1/D2, GERM 202 or equivalents, from high school, CEGEP, electives or extra courses.
1038-performance: 10 and 9 credits from two lists; 400–500 level MUEN up to 4. MUEN courses can repeat.
1038-program-description: Practical and theoretical training, with lessons, chamber music, and large ensembles such as the Symphony Orchestra, Contemporary Music Ensemble and Wind Orchestra. 91 credits, plus 34 Foundation for out-of-province students.
1038-special-requirements: B- minimum in practical instruction, exams and ensembles. Violin, viola and cello start with two terms of MUEN 565.
1039-performance-2: 12 credits of large ensembles and 4 of small, by audition, plus 9 from the list (400–500 level MUEN up to 4). Percussionists must include MUEN 569, MUPG 328 and MUPG 329.
1040-program-description: Historical practice and period instruments: lessons, ensembles, workshops, master classes, lectures and research. 91 credits, plus 34 Foundation for out-of-province students.
